newsitem.title: HUNGARY: PHILIP WITNESSES BEAVER REINTRODUCTION TO HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: PHILIP WITNESSES BEAVER REINTRODUCTION TO HUNGARY.

text.p: Britain's Prince Philip presided on Monday over the introduction of a five-member family of Austrian beavers to a section of the Danube in southern Hungary, Hungarian news agency MTI reported.
The beavers were released into the Danube-Drava National Park near Hungary's border with Serbia by the WorldWide Fund for Nature"s (WWF), of which Philip is Honorary President.
Beavers were common to Hungary until the 19th century but were then driven out by fur hunters.

The Hungarian branch of WWF launched the re-introduction programme in June 1996 when it released two other three-member Austrian beaver families successfully into the wild in another section of the park.
Prince Philip enquired as to the environment's suitability as a beaver habitat and was reassured by local experts, MTI said.
